record.original_question: Can one find a Hardy-field function a(t) with super-polynomial growth, meaning a(t)/t^k → ∞ for every k, such that the integer sequence [a(n)] is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers?

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Find an example of a function a ∈ H that grows faster than polynomials, meaning, a(t)/tk → ∞ for every k ∈ N, such that the sequence [a(n)] is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote a Hardy field, that is, a field (under pointwise addition and multiplication) of germs at $+\infty$ of real-valued functions defined on half-lines $[c,\infty)$, closed under differentiation. For $a\in\mathcal{H}$, write $[a(n)]$ for the sequence of integer parts $\lfloor a(n)\rfloor$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

A sequence of integers $(b_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is said to be good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers if, for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A)>0$, one has
$$\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mu\!\left(A\cap T^{-b_n}A\cap T^{-2b_n}A\cap\cdots\cap T^{-kb_n}A\right)>0,$$
and, moreover, for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $f_1,\dots,f_k\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f_1(T^{b_n}x)\,f_2(T^{2b_n}x)\cdots f_k(T^{kb_n}x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$.

The function $a\in\mathcal{H}$ is said to have super-polynomial growth if $a(t)/t^k\to\infty$ as $t\to\infty$ for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$.

Question: Does there exist a function $a\in\mathcal{H}$ of super-polynomial growth such that the integer sequence $([a(n)])_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers in the sense above?
artifact.category_tag: Hardy field sequences and multiple recurrence
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works on multiple recurrence and convergence for Hardy field sequences (e.g., Frantzikinakis–Host 2020, and follow-ups on Furstenberg systems of Hardy sequences) treat the polynomial-growth regime; results allowing super-polynomial growth have been pursued (notably a 2025 preprint on Furstenberg systems of certain super-polynomial Hardy sequences), but no published result is found explicitly producing a super-polynomial Hardy function whose integer parts are good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers in full generality. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field (Frantzikinakis–Host)
status_evidence.snippet: Results assume the Hardy field functions have polynomial growth.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art convergence/recurrence results for Hardy sequences are restricted to polynomial growth.

status_evidence.title: Furstenberg systems of certain sequences of superpolynomial growth
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Furstenberg systems associated with Hardy sequences of super-polynomial growth.
status_evidence.claim: Super-polynomial Hardy sequences are an active topic, with partial structural results, but the multiple recurrence/convergence-of-powers question is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems on multiple ergodic averages (Frantzikinakis)
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems on multiple ergodic averages including questions on Hardy sequences.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems on multiple ergodic averages.
